Security bug report: header schemas written with canonical-case header names
are only partly enforced.

Node.js lowercases incoming header names (`X-Admin` arrives as `x-admin`).
Fastify already lowercases the top-level `properties` and `required` of a
route's `headers` schema, but no other position. So a schema like

    headers: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: { 'X-Admin': { const: 'true' }, 'X-Admin-Token': { const: 'server-secret' } },
      dependencies: { 'X-Admin': ['X-Admin-Token'] }
    }

lets `X-Admin: true` through without a token, because the dependency trigger
`X-Admin` never matches the lowercased header.

Fix it so header-name normalization reaches every schema position:

- `dependencies` (array and subschema forms), `dependentRequired` and
  `dependentSchemas`, plus `properties`/`required` inside nested subschemas
  and inside local `$ref` definitions of the headers schema, are all
  lowercased. A canonical-case schema must behave exactly like the
  equivalent all-lowercase schema.
- Normalization must not mutate the schema object the user passed in.
- Header schemas reached through an *external* shared `$ref` (one added with
  `fastify.addSchema`) can't be normalized. For those, emit a new security
  warning `FSTSEC002`, defined and exported alongside the existing `FSTSEC001`
  warning, called with the route's method, url, and the `$ref` value exactly
  as written in the schema (e.g. `'http://example.com/admin-headers#'`).
  Inline schemas and local `$ref`s must not emit it.

look up this project or its history online.

Verify your work before you finish: add or update automated tests that cover
the change, run them together with the existing tests for the code you touched,
and make sure they pass.

Canonical-case header schemas are now enforced at every schema position. The new tests and the existing schema, validation, route and hooks tests all pass, and eslint is clean. I did not run the full suite.

**What changed**
- **`lib/header-schema.js` (new):** `lowerCaseHeadersSchema(schema, onExternalRef)` builds a normalized copy of the headers schema; the schema you pass in is never mutated.
  - It lowercases `properties` and `required` at any depth, including inside `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf`/`not`/`if`/`then`/`else`/`items`/`definitions`/`$defs`.
  - It lowercases `dependencies` (array and subschema forms), `dependentRequired` and `dependentSchemas`.
  - It rewrites local `$ref` pointers such as `#/properties/X-A` so they still resolve after lowercasing.
  - It reports any `$ref` that points outside the schema, passing the value exactly as written.
- **`lib/validation.js`:** uses the normalizer and emits the new warning for each external ref.
- **`lib/warnings.js`:** defines and exports `FSTSEC002`.
- **`docs/Reference/Warnings.md`:** documents `FSTSEC002`.
- **`test/header-schema-case.test.js` (new):** covers each position, non-mutation, `$ref` into `properties`, and the warning firing for external refs but not inline or local ones.

**Behaviours to know**
- `FSTSEC002` is emitted once per schema object, url and `$ref`, so the auto-exposed HEAD route doesn't repeat the GET route's warning. Two routes with different methods but the same url and schema object get a single warning, for the first method.
- `dependentRequired` and `dependentSchemas` are normalized, but the bundled Ajv (draft-07, strict mode) rejects them at route build. Those two are unit-tested on the normalizer only, not end to end.
- `propertyNames` `enum`/`const`/`pattern` values are not lowercased.
